lessons.title: Bits and Binary
intro: Every byte is made of 8 bits, each one 0 or 1. Written in binary with a % in front, $0A is %00001010.
The bits are numbered 7 to 0 from left to right, and each is worth double the one to its right: 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. %00001010 is 8 + 2 = 10.
One hex digit is exactly 4 bits. That's why programmers love hex: $A5 is %1010 0101, one digit per half byte.

exercises.explanation: F is %1111 and 0 is %0000. Each hex digit becomes 4 bits.

exercises.prompt: Load A with 3, written in binary.
Why is bit 7 special on the 6502?
options: It's copied into the N flag
exercises.explanation: When bit 7 is 1, the value is $80 or more, and N = 1.

exercises.prompt: How many bits does one hex digit stand for?
exercises.explanation: 16 values need 4 bits. Two hex digits make a whole byte.

lessons.title: AND: Masking
intro: AND #value compares A with the value bit by bit. A bit stays 1 only where both are 1. Everywhere else the result is 0.
That makes AND a mask: AND #%00001111 keeps the lower 4 bits and clears the upper 4. AND #$0F turns $3C into $0C.
It's also a quick test: AND #1 leaves 1 for odd numbers and 0 for even ones, and the Z flag tells you which.

output: A = $0C (only the lower half is left)

exercises.explanation: Only the leftmost bit is 1 in both.

exercises.prompt: What is A after LDA #$F7 and AND #$0F?
exercises.explanation: The upper 4 bits are cleared, the lower 4 ($7) stay.

exercises.prompt: A holds 9. What is the Z flag after AND #1?
exercises.explanation: 9 is %00001001. Bit 0 is set, so the result is 1 and Z = 0.

exercises.prompt: Keep only the lower 4 bits of A.
exercises.explanation: $0F is %00001111: ones in the lower half, zeros in the upper half.

exercises.prompt: This should keep the upper half of $AB ($A0), but gives $0B. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: $0F keeps the lower half. For the upper half use AND #$F0.
No bit is 1 in both, so every bit becomes 0.

lessons.title: ORA and EOR
intro: ORA #value sets bits: a bit becomes 1 if it's 1 in A or in the value. ORA #%10000000 switches bit 7 on, without touching the others.
EOR #value (exclusive or) flips bits: where the value has a 1, the bit in A turns over. EOR #$FF flips all 8 bits.
So: AND clears bits, ORA sets bits, EOR flips bits. With these three you can change any single bit of a byte.

exercises.explanation: A bit is 1 if it's 1 in either of them.
EOR gives 1 where the two are different.

exercises.prompt: What is A after LDA #$0F and EOR #$FF?
Switch bit 0 on, without changing the other bits.
exercises.explanation: ORA #1 sets bit 0. EOR would flip it off again if it was already on.

exercises.prompt: You want to switch a lamp bit on and off each time. Which instruction fits?
exercises.explanation: EOR flips the bit: on becomes off, off becomes on.

exercises.prompt: Set bit 7 of the byte at $30, then store it back.
exercises.explanation: Read, set the bit, write back.
